metadata.title: Understanding Chinese Students' Well-Being: A Machine Learning Study

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 data for Mainland China, restricted to students from Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang (B-S-J-Z) and to 15-year-olds in grade 9–10. The manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling/student weights or any replicate-weight scheme, and it does not name any weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or variance estimation approach. Because the primary model is a random forest regression, the authors do not describe a weight-aware ML estimation procedure; thus, the analysis should be treated as potentially unweighted with respect to complex survey design. Analysts using the OECD PISA microdata should consider whether to apply PISA sampling weights and appropriate replicate methods when estimating uncertainty, especially given the nested structure (students within schools within regions).

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the dependent variables are well-being dimensions measured directly from questionnaire Likert items (positive affect, negative affect, life satisfaction, and meaning in life), not PV-based cognitive achievement scores. The study instead imputes missing questionnaire responses using MCMC multiple imputation, which is appropriate for item-level survey data. Therefore, PV-specific handling is not part of the analysis pipeline for these outcomes.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 Mainland China data publicly available from the OECD. The analytic sample consists of 12,058 15-year-old students from the four core regions Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang (B-S-J-Z). The paper reports the grade composition (majority in grade 10 and grade 9) but does not describe additional task/module restrictions beyond using the PISA 2018 questionnaire constructs listed in Table 1. Missing values on the included variables were imputed using MCMC multiple imputation prior to the primary ML analysis.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Mainland China (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang) — 15-year-olds — Subjective well-being: Positive affect
main_findings.performance_metrics: Random Forest regression — R²: 21.41% (MSE: 0.79) for the full 35-factor model; optimal top-9 model R²: 21.41% (MSE: 0.79) reported as best via repeated 10-fold cross-validation.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Mainland China data (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang) for 15-year-olds, the study leveraged resilience, reading self-concept competence, work mastery, mastery goal orientation, and sense of school belonging to predict positive affect, finding that school belonging and resilience were the most important predictors (ranked 1st and 2nd among the selected top predictors). This indicates that strengthening students’ sense of belonging and resilience through school climate and student-support interventions may be a high-leverage strategy for improving positive emotional well-being, though the cross-sectional design prevents causal claims.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Mainland China (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang) — 15-year-olds — Subjective well-being: Negative affect
main_findings.performance_metrics: Random Forest regression — R²: 19.21% (MSE: 0.81) overall; top-9 dominant model R²: 18.13% (MSE: 0.82) reported as the selected negative-affect model via repeated 10-fold cross-validation.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Mainland China data (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang) for 15-year-olds, the study leveraged sense of school belonging, general fear of failure, resilience, reading for enjoyment, and reading self-concept competence to predict negative affect, finding that fear of failure and school belonging were the most important predictors (ranked 1st and 2nd among the selected top predictors). This indicates that interventions reducing students’ fear of failure (e.g., feedback and assessment practices) and improving school belonging may help lower negative emotional experiences, while causality cannot be inferred from the cross-sectional ML prediction.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Mainland China (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang) — 15-year-olds — Subjective well-being: Life satisfaction
main_findings.performance_metrics: Random Forest regression — R²: 26.44% (MSE: 0.74) for the overall 35-factor model; selected top-9 model R²: 24.14% (MSE: 0.76).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Mainland China data (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang) for 15-year-olds, the study leveraged sense of school belonging, resilience, parents’ emotional support, fear of failure, and work mastery to predict life satisfaction, finding that school belonging and resilience were the most important predictors (ranked 1st and 2nd among the selected top predictors). This indicates that policies and school practices that foster belonging and resilience—along with supportive parent–student relationships—may improve students’ cognitive evaluations of their lives, though the study’s design remains non-causal.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Mainland China (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang) — 15-year-olds — Eudaimonic well-being: Meaning in life
main_findings.performance_metrics: Random Forest regression — R²: 32.47% (MSE: 0.68) for the overall 35-factor model; selected top-9 model R²: 32.47% (MSE: 0.78) reported for the final selected model via repeated 10-fold cross-validation.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Mainland China data (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang) for 15-year-olds, the study leveraged resilience, work mastery, cooperation at school, parents’ emotional support, and sense of school belonging to predict eudaimonic well-being (meaning in life), finding that resilience and work mastery were the most important predictors (ranked 1st and 2nd among the selected top predictors). This indicates that building students’ capacity to cope with adversity (resilience) and to feel mastery in work/learning may be central for enhancing meaning and purpose, while the cross-sectional ML approach does not establish causal mechanisms.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2018 questionnaire data for 12,058 Chinese 15-year-olds from Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang (B-S-J-Z), predicting four well-being dimensions: positive affect, negative affect, life satisfaction, and eudaimonic well-being (meaning in life). Missing responses were handled via MCMC multiple imputation, and all variables were standardized before modeling. The primary method was random forest regression, evaluated with repeated 10-fold cross-validation; the models explained about 21.41% (positive affect), 19.21% (negative affect), 26.44% (life satisfaction), and 32.47% (eudaimonic well-being) of variance in the respective outcomes. Across outcomes, school belonging and resilience were consistently central, while fear of failure was especially important for negative affect and resilience/work mastery dominated eudaimonic well-being. The paper does not report applying PISA sampling/replicate weights, and the cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation of ML feature importance.
